sources.title: MIVUBI Loot Drop Pickup and Economy Transfer Policy v1

facts.subject: reward source
facts.statement: Every gameplay reward path must be classified and registered: ENGINE_LOOT_TABLE, LOOT_COMMAND, SCRIPT_INVENTORY_GRANT, DROPPED_ITEM_PICKUP, SCOREBOARD_CURRENCY, STRUCTURE_CONTAINER, or RECOVERY_REWARD. Multiple paths for the same logical reward require explicit arbitration.

facts.subject: logical reward
facts.statement: A logical reward must carry rewardOperationId, arenaGeneration, round/result id where applicable, recipient identity/session generation, source, and expected value so retries or parallel loot/script paths cannot commit it twice.

facts.subject: dropped arena item
facts.statement: Arena-relevant dropped items should have explicit logical ownership or correlatable metadata for arenaGeneration, rewardOperationId, allowed recipients/team, and expiry/cleanup policy. Ambient item entities must not be indistinguishable from protected gameplay rewards.

facts.subject: item pickup eligibility
facts.statement: Before a pickup produces gameplay currency/progression/objective credit, validate picker session, arena/team scope, drop generation, reward ownership, and item identity. A successful engine pickup alone does not prove gameplay eligibility.

facts.subject: reward transfer capacity
facts.statement: Reward systems that require inventory delivery must define behavior when inventory cannot fully accept the reward: keep/drop remainder, mailbox/defer, convert, reject, or compensate. Currency/progression must not commit as if physical delivery succeeded when delivery is required.

facts.subject: pickup economy commit
facts.statement: For pickup-to-currency conversions, use a single transaction order: validate drop/picker, reserve claim idempotently, verify pickup/inventory or consume/remove according to mode, then commit currency/progression. Avoid incrementing currency while leaving a claimable item in the world.

facts.subject: death reward paths
facts.statement: If entity death can produce an engine loot table and script-side kill reward, declare whether they are complementary or mutually exclusive. Equivalent rewards from both paths are a duplicate-reward defect.

facts.subject: round-end dropped item
facts.statement: Drops owned by an ending arena generation must be removed, expired, or made ineligible before the next generation starts. A round-N item picked up in round N+1 must not grant round-N reward semantics.

facts.subject: loot table integrity
facts.statement: For gameplay-critical loot tables, analyzer should resolve referenced table paths, pools, conditions, nested references, multiplicity, and overlap with scripted reward logic before concluding that a missing or duplicate reward is an inventory bug.

facts.subject: terminal reward
facts.statement: Durable end-of-round rewards remain gated by RESULT_COMMITTED and reuse the round/result reward operation token; dropped cosmetic or intermediate loot must not bypass terminal reward idempotency when representing the same entitlement.

facts.subject: arena cleanup
facts.statement: Arena cleanup must reconcile both dropped item entities and their originating reward/spawner paths, including containers restored by structure, delayed loot commands, scripted drops, and death loot sources, before declaring the arena reusable.
